subject: Acme: Feature parity and next steps (streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme: Feature parity and next steps (streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Great to connect this morning — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery and the competitive topics you raised (Azure/OAI / Bedrock comparisons). I want to make sure the next tests focus on the things that matter to your engineering team:

Key priorities you called out:
- Reliable streaming (token-by-token updates + partial payloads)
- Function/tool-calling compatibility (your internal KB + vector search integration)
- Strict structured outputs (JSON schema validation and rerun behavior)
- Latency SLOs and cost per 1k tokens targets for production traffic

Proposed immediate next tests (attached test plan):
1) Streaming behavior: run a 2k-turn prompt set that exercises partial responses, early-stop behavior, and reconnections. Measure token-latency and ordering.
2) Function/tool calling: exercise calls to your KB retrieval endpoint and a mocked third-party tool (we'll run a small integration harness).
3) Structured outputs: evaluate strict JSON schema enforcement across different model variants and our streaming parser.

Success criteria (suggested):
- Streaming: consistent token ordering, max token-latency < 100ms for median on our dedicated config
- Tool-calling: 100% correct function signature detection for sample set; successful round-trip to KB for >95% of queries
- Structured: schema validation pass rate > 98% or graceful fallback with deterministic error payload

Next steps / asks for your team:
- Can you provide a short list of 10 representative prompts (both short and long form) and an example KB endpoint (staging credentials) so our SE can run the tool-calling tests?
- Confirm whether we should run tests on hosted API (quick) or a dedicated/private trial instance (closer to production).

I'll loop Dev in to scope the integration test and propose dates. Attaching the feature-parity test plan and sample data.

Pls let me know if I misunderstood any priorities. Happy to sync for 30m tomorrow to align.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: acme-feature-parity-test-plan.pdf

From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme: Feature parity and next steps (streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the test plan. That aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications and priorities from our side:

1) Streaming is the top priority — we saw flaky partial responses when we tried streaming via Azure OpenAI and a few issues on Bedrock. We need to validate token-level ordering and reconnection semantics.
2) Tool-calling: for the POC please prioritize our KB integration first (KB host: kb-staging.acme.internal) — we'll share a short-lived API key. We also want to test how Redwood surfaces tool call failures and retries.
3) Structured outputs: we have strict schemas for our billing export and invoice-parsing flows — please validate both strict and relaxed parsing modes.

Timeline: if possible, we'd like to run tests next week (Aug 18-20). Can you confirm availability and whether you need a dedicated instance?

Also: curious on how Redwood compares to the hyperscalers on cost for continuous streaming workloads — if you have a quick delta table or examples that would be useful for our finance team.

Thanks — attaching the 10 sample prompts we discussed.

Best,
Sam Ortiz
Head of AI Integrations | Acme Corp
sam.ortiz@acme.com | +1 212-555-0199

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme: Feature parity and next steps (streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs)

Thanks Sam — good notes. Per your ask, we put together a focused test bundle and attached the streaming-test-suite.jsonl and a small tool-calling sample harness (tool-calling-sample.zip). Outline below and proposed sequencing so we can hit your Aug 18-20 window: 

Planned test sequence:
1) Streaming validation (Aug 18 morning) — Redwood SE will run the streaming-test-suite to measure token latencies, ordering, reconnection behavior, and partial payloads. We will run this on both our hosted cluster and a dedicated Dev instance so you can compare behavior.
2) Tool-calling integration (Aug 18 afternoon) — Dev Patel will run calls against your KB staging endpoint and validate function signature detection + failure/retry behavior. We'll use the sample harness in the zip and can swap in your staging URL and API key.
3) Structured outputs (Aug 19) — run the strict/relaxed schema checks across the sample prompts you shared; we'll surface pass rates and examples for any failures.

Success metrics and deliverables:
- Per-test summary (pass/fail), token latency percentiles, and a short narrative comparing to common hyperscaler patterns we see (e.g., streaming behavior differences, tooling around function-calls).
- A short recording of the SE run and a reproducible script you can run in your CI.

Scheduling: I put a 30m SE sync on my Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood-se/30min - can you pick a slot on Aug 17 or morning of Aug 18? We'll plan a 1hr hands-on test session Aug 18 if that works.

Attachments: streaming-test-suite.jsonl, tool-calling-sample.zip

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme: Feature parity and next steps (streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs)

Hi Sam / Priya —

I'm available for the hands-on session and I've drafted the technical checklist so we can run the tests efficiently. A few things I need from you before the 18th session:

Required from Acme before test run:
- Short-lived staging API key for kb-staging.acme.internal (scoped to read-only)
- Example webhooks or tool endpoint behavior (error codes, retry windows) if you have special handling
- Confirmation whether we should run against Redwood hosted API or provision a short-lived Dedicated trial (Dedicated will give more production-like latency but takes ~2 hours to provision)

Technical checklist (what we'll execute during the session):
- Streaming: cURL + WS tests against streaming endpoint (we'll run 50 sample prompts from the provided jsonl and capture per-token timestamps)
  - Endpoint: https://api.redwood.com/v1/streaming/generate
  - Models to test: redwood-stream-2, redwood-compat-1, and a quantized low-latency variant
- Tool-calling: run harness from tool-calling-sample.zip; validate function_signature detection and simulated KB round-trips. We'll capture failure modes and our automatic fallback behavior.
- Structured outputs: run strict-json validator and a relaxed mode that returns an errors array + stable parse.

Deliverables post-session:
- Test artifact bundle (logs + jsonl results)
- Short analysis doc comparing Redwood observed behavior to typical hyperscaler patterns for streaming and function-calls

If you can share the staging key and an initial 5 prompts with expected outputs by EOD tomorrow (Aug 18 09:00 PDT), we'll be able to run the full suite in the planned window. Otherwise we can shift to provisioning Dedicated and run late Aug 18.

Ping me on Slack (dev.patel@redwood.slack.com) if you want to share creds securely.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0188
